newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian princess visits Burmese first lady.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian princess visits Burmese first lady.

text.p: Princess Marie, wife of Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, left on Friday for a three-day visit to Burma's first lady, officials said.
Members of Ranariddh's cabinet told Reuters that the princess had made the trip at the invitation of Daw Kyaing Kyaing, wife of Burma's military ruler, General Than Shwe.

"There are a lot of common points between the two nations -- future members of ASEAN, from the same region, two countries developing their own economies," said Xavier d'Abzac, advisor to Ranariddh, noting the visit would strengthen relations between the two nations.

Cambodia is scheduled to join the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) at the same time as Burma. Both countries have observer status in ASEAN, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
The visit follows a trip to Cambodia by Than Shwe and Daw Kyaing Kyaing in October, when Burma signed air transport and tourism agreements with Cambodia.
That trip drew protests from Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy, who led a demonstration in support of pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi during the visit.

But government leaders said it is not Cambodia's place to interfere in the internal politics of Burma, where Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy, which won elections in 1990 but was not allowed to take power, continues to oppose the military government, the State Law and Order Restoration Council.
